utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-14-R77.2, the Prosecutor versus Ivica Marijacic and Markica Rebic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I take the appearances from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. David Akerson on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm here with Rebecca Graham, Salvatore Cannata, and Sebastian van Hooydonk, who is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Akerson. I wonder if the Defence is following this procedure. Can I take the appearance for the Defence for Mr. Marijacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Marin Ivanovic, attorney at law in Zagreb, and I represent Mr. Marijacic in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivanovic. Then appearances for the accused, Mr. Rebic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, I'm Kresimir Krsnik. I'm a member of the Croat bar association and I represent Mr. Rebic, and I'm joined by Mr. Miljevic as co-counsel and we've got a legal assistant, Cosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder, both the Accused are also present there? Mr. Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, both Mr. Marijacic and Mr. Rebic are present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krsnik. First of all, I have to not that today's hearing is being held by telephone link with the Defence for both accused participating from the ICTY Field Office in Zagreb Croatia. Since it is the first time for me to have a hearing in the form of a telephone conference, I think I need to understand the implication of the technical setting. My understanding is that the interpreters in the courtroom will interpret simultaneously, as usual, but that the Defence, however, will follow the procedure only in B/C/S. Since it is not possible to see the person who is speaking, I would ask the interpreters to kindly identify the speaker who is speaking before they start to interpret his or her words so that the participants can follow who is the speaker. And also, it is important for the Defence, who are now in Zagreb, to identify themselves before they speak. Do you follow, Mr. Ivanovic and Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We can hear everything very well. We do have a special conference phone and we are all able to follow the proceedings perfectly, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Also, it would be very important, I think, under this situation for every speaker to put a pause before he starts to speak. Having said that, I'll turn to our agenda for today. Today's hearing is a Status Conference, being held for the first time since the initial appearance which took place in 14th of June this year. Yesterday, the Chamber issued four decisions denying certification for appeal against the decision on the motions to amend the indictment and the decision on motions to dismiss the indictment due to lack of jurisdiction. By this, I think all the preliminary motions filed by both parties have been resolved and there are no pending motions. Under the circumstances of this case, therefore, I scheduled today's hearing to check if the case is ready for trial and, further, thereafter, explore the possible trial dates. First of all, I'd like to turn to the issue of disclosure. In the meantime, as for indictment, the Prosecution filed the amended indictment on 14th October 2005, following the Trial Chamber's decision on the motion to amend the indictment. At the Initial Appearance in June, the Prosecution stated that Rule 66(A)(i) disclosure would be completed the very morning, the next morning. Can I confirm with the Prosecution that disclosure was completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there was some confusion. The disclosure that we were referring to, and maybe this might be my error, was disclosure of the supporting materials at that point. We are planning to provide Rule 66(A) disclosure on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I had in mind the 66(A)(i) supporting materials and the order. So now we are going to deal with 66(A)(ii) but we have to deal first of all with how many witnesses the Prosecution is going to call for the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Maximum of six witnesses. We expect it to be lower but at the moment that would be the maximum number of witnesses, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Akerson, to be frank, I don't follow your words. Maximum six, so given this more important issue would be legal matter than factual matter. What witnesses do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: One of the issues in this trial, Your Honour, based on the Trial Chamber's ruling on our motion to amend is that we have to prove that an order of the court was violated. There are three relevant orders in this case, and one of the aspects that we need to prove is potentially the application of these orders to the Accused. So we have to call witnesses to establish, pertaining to the 1997 order in the Blaskic case, that it would apply to these Accused. That is not by the way our only legal theory but that is one of the legal theories, that the orders must be directed to these Accused and so we have a factual determination that we have to prove and that has to be established by a witness who can say -- the 1997 order by the way states that the order applies to the Blaskic Defence counsel and their representatives, and that is a matter of proof for us to show that these Accused fall within that category of people, and so we are going to need to call witnesses to establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, how many witnesses do you need for that fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: If I could have one moment, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the legal team is trying to locate the witness list as it currently exists. Off of memory, I'm going it tell the Court I think there are two witnesses, if memory serves me, that are listed for that basis. We have two witnesses that are foundational witnesses for the exhibits that we intend to admit into court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow. Why do you need a witness or witnesses to lay foundation on the orders? Do they not speak for themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Not for the orders; these are other exhibits. We have exhibits relevant to the proof of the 1997 order and the relationship.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the -- to prove that one of the Accused is -- can be classified as a representative of counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you need two witnesses and exhibits to prove that fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: We need two witnesses. There are multiple exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: -- regarding that. There is a number of exhibits that we will need to introduce to prove that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And other four witnesses, when you say a maximum six, what are they for?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: One is our lead investigator in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's going to testify on what field?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: He conducted the investigation as to the article. There is a previous publication to the article that is going to need to be discussed. He has also investigated the employment of Mr. Marijacic at another newspaper in the year 2000 that's relevant to this case because one of the other orders that's applicable to this case was served on the Slobodna Dalmacija newspaper while Mr. Marijacic was an employee there. And he can testify just generally to the background of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if you could go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you've dealt with one, two, three, four, five, so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: And one other OTP employee, who is a member of our legal research team, and her responsibility is to monitor all public record documents, newspapers, and she's also listed as a foundational witness to establish the authenticity and admissibility of the newspapers. Based on stipulations by Defence counsel which we've discussed verbally but we are going to submitted in writing we may not need foundational witnesses in this case. But as of right now I have to list them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, I'm wondering whether the OTP needs all of these witnesses but on the one hand, the Chamber will consider this matter in due course, but I would very much encourage to reduce the number on the part of the OTP as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: And we would share that concern and we will make every effort to try to trim down our witness list. But since we only got the Court's decision, the Trial Chamber's decision on the certification we've only had a few days to figure out our legal strategy as the indictment is currently amended. So that will -- we'll get more clarity on that in the coming days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I had in mind the Prosecution would have only one or two witnesses at maximum, but we'll see. How long would you expect the Prosecution case to last overall?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Maximum of five days, probably less. But maximum of five days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're surprising me.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has in mind that all the trial would last not more than two days but we'll see. So you have statements of these -- all of these witnesses? So that they can be disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Whatever statements we have will be disclosed. Some of these witnesses won't have statements but if a witness has a statement, we will of course disclose that. For a foundational witness, for instance, we are not going to produce a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You once mentioned an expert but you're not minded to call an expert this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: No, we are not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And when do you think complete your 66(A)(ii) disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: We plan to submit that on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Monday meaning next Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Monday being 31st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I will trust the Court's calendar because I don't have one in front of me. But I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me say again, we have an article which says everything, and I understand the Prosecution wishes to call witnesses who may say that Mr. Rebic or Marijacic can be said to be a representative of the Defence or something, but I still have difficulty following why the Prosecution needs all these "foundational" witnesses. I would urge Mr. Akerson to think it over again but -- and as for pre-trial brief, since this trial contains these legal matters, I would -- I think it would be advantageous to have a written submission in the files, in the form of pre-trial brief, and when do you think you can file the pre-trial brief, Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: We plan to file that as well on Monday, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The 31st. That's good. Thank you, Mr. Akerson. Can I now turn to Mr. Ivanovic and Mr. Krsnik? How many witnesses do you envisage for trial? If Mr. Ivanovic could speak first.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is Marin Ivanovic speaking. According to our current assessment -- well, we haven't looked into this in great detail because we've received a decision from this Court only today, the decision which rejects our own proposals. We're still at the preparatory stage, we're still proofing the witnesses. And according to our current plan, we are counting on five witnesses at most. But following the Prosecution I think we will have to give it some more thought and ponder some additional details, as I said in the light of what we just heard from the Prosecution, in order to decide whether we need any extra witnesses or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What would be the point of those five witnesses, at least five witnesses, would lead us to?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically it would be expert witnesses or, rather, witnesses on the basis of position and the respect they enjoy are qualified to appear as foundational witnesses and they would be in a position to testify as to the potential relationship. First of all, between Mr. Marijacic and the ones that the order for 1997 refers to, as well as other evidence, I mean we'll have to wait for the disclosure from the Prosecution in order to be able to say anything more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivanovic, if you could elaborate on expert, what expertise do you need for this trial? Do you have in mind legal Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. submissions, legal expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do apologise. This is Marin Ivanovic again. First and foremost, legal experts who would be in a position to indicate how this fits within different legal systems, the indictment against Mr. Marijacic and all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, I wonder why -- whether we need a legal expert to deal with the legal issues. Why do you -- why are you not able to deal with it in the form of your submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Marin Ivanovic again. Of course we are going to do that. But as to individual theories and comparisons with regard to provisions within other bodies of law that are not always familiar with is going to be left up to the experts, expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. And the other witnesses than this expert will be testifying on what matters? If I can ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Marin Ivanovic again. As the Prosecution officials said earlier on in the course of this Status Conference, is going to be looking into the relationship between Marijacic and the Defence team for which General Blaskic. Once we've seen that, we'll certainly be in a position to see whether we'll need to call any witnesses. For the time being I can't really say anything more because we haven't seen any of those documents from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. If Mr. Krsnik has anything to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Certainly. First of all, I would like to stress that we have not received disclosures as yet apart from the supporting materials. So this is the first point I'd like to make. Once we've seen that we'll be able to start working on witnesses. At the present moment, quite frankly, I can't begin to tell you how many we'll have for Mr. Rebic. In fact we are rather surprised to hear what the Prosecution has to say, and their learned colleagues on the Prosecution. But on the one hand we're pleased about that because they are simply confirming the thesis put forward by the Defence. That is to say that, in as far as contempt of court is concerned it is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note Mr. Akerson is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Akerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting, Your Honour but I've just been told that the Court Reporter is not getting the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There is a switch which can turn down the B/C/S. Now is it okay? Mr. Krsnik, if you can say a word so that the court recorder can confirm he can listen to -- he can follow the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, what I was trying to say is that we were rather pleased that our learned colleagues from the Prosecution have -- is it okay? Can you follow now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Krsnik, I have to clarify one thing. You said you haven't received the supporting material yet but you received the so-called supporting material which accompanied the indictment, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. We did receive the supporting material but we have not received anything according to Rule 66 bis -- 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you will receive them next week on Monday, as was noted by Mr. Akerson. And proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Your Honour, but you know how essential it is for the Defence to analyse such materials very carefully because that's what our Defence strategy is based on. At the present moment, quite frankly, I'm not in a position to tell you how many witnesses we will have to call. I don't suppose very many. Roughly speaking, I can tell you that since this is mostly about legal issues, we'll have witnesses from the legal profession. And to come back to the points I was making earlier when I was interrupted, as I said, we were rather surprised but also very pleased to hear the attitude of our learned colleagues from the Prosecution. It simply confirms the point that the Defence has been making from the very start, that is to say that this contempt of court issue is very questionable so to say with regard to a third party, especially if we are talking about journalists, and I can see now that they are trying to establish a link between them and the Defence team. This is a new development from our point of view. And we shall certainly have to develop our Defence strategy along those lines, and, of course, trying to prove the opposite. And unfortunately, I have to say that rather than basing it all on reasonable doubt, we'll have to counteract this on the basis of proving the truth. Your Honour, that's all we have to say on behalf of Mr. Rebic. I don't know whether my colleague, Miljevic would like to add anything. Yes, my colleague, Mr. Miljevic, would like to say a few words. So if you allow him to take the floor he'd very much like to do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krsnik. Mr. Miljevic, do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Veljko Miljevic. I do, just very briefly. On the basis of what we've heard so far and according to Rule 66, the Prosecution has lived up to its obligations according to Rule 66(A)(i). However, they did not act in line with their obligations on the basis of Rule 66(A)(ii), nor indeed 66(B). Only at such time when the Prosecution fully complies with their duties on the basis of Rule 66(A)(ii) and 66(B) shall we be in a position to get a decision on the part of the Trial Chamber with regard to Rule 73 bis(C), and that has to do with the number of witnesses that the Prosecution is allowed to call and the amount of time that they will have available for their evidence. Once we find out about that, and I suppose we are likely to find out as early as Monday, as I said only when we find out about that shall we be able to tell you how many witnesses we'll call, and certainly we'll have less witnesses than the number suggested by the Prosecution, and called by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Having heard from the Prosecution that they are going to complete their 66(A)(ii) disclosure and that they will file their pre-trial brief on next Monday, the 31st of October, how long would the Defence need to submit their pre-trial brief? Can I hear from Mr. Ivanovic first?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Marin Ivanovic. Your Honour, we are unable to tell you at the present moment. Once the Prosecution has complied with their duties, we shall study the relevant materials and then we will make our decision. However, I would like to stress that according to the current state of affairs, we'll certainly have to ask for assistance from this Trial Chamber in terms of subpoenas being issued in order to get certain pieces of evidence. If we can get that, I think we shall need an appropriate period of time in order to do all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I hear from you more about that subpoena? If necessary, we can go --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Marin Ivanovic. Perhaps we could go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it possible under this setting and telephone conference? Yes. Yes, we will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session again. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Marin Ivanovic again. I don't know where the learned colleague from the Prosecution found the information to lead him to think that we can arrive at a stipulation, but what I was saying quite simply was that we might need some assistance from the Court in getting those documents. However, if the Prosecution have that information and if they are kind enough to submit it to us, we will be extremely pleased and, of course, we won't have to seek assistance from the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I take the floor now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are in open session, I think we have to be careful but I think we'll understand one another. It is about a crucial issue here but it is rather simple and straightforward. This supposedly published article is not a part of the transcript from the trial and so this is the crucial issue because this allegedly published article deals with something else and not the actual transcript from the trial. I do agree and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We've lost the sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can follow you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Continue, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what was the last point that you heard because unfortunately I have no way of following what you are hearing up there in the courtroom. But I was trying to emphasise the crucial difference between the status of the witness, because this allegedly published article was not a part of the transcript from the trial, and it had nothing to do with the status of the witness in the course of the trial, but there is a difference between the status of the witness in the course of the trial and in the course of the investigation. Because this allegedly published article conditionally speaking refers to the investigation stage, when, according to the opinion of the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt for a minute? Mr. Akerson the indictment alleges that the accused published the statement as well as transcript, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: The indictment, Your Honour, sets forth the publication of the statement, not the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: But if I can just add, Your Honour, I think we are getting into matters that are to be litigated at trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: What we are trying to decide today -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because we are dealing with the number of witnesses so we will touch upon very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what our objections have all been about, that was the whole point of our motions from day 1. And I apologise if I'm wrong. I wouldn't like you to misunderstand me, but I have the impression that the Prosecution is trying to avoid answering this question because it does state in the indictment that the article published the statement from the main trial, which is totally untrue. And as the Defence team, we have to sort that one out. And we are willing to talk to the Prosecution and to reach some form of agreement in case they are willing to renounce this form of indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, Mr. Akerson is on his feet. Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I'll just read the applicable provisions of the indictment, Your Honour, and I think this will clarify. Paragraph 10 of the third amended indictment, which is the current indictment, states that "Mr. Marijacic knowingly and willingly -- wilfully interfered with the administration of justice in three respects by publishing the identity of the protected witness, the statement of the witness, and the fact that the witness had testified in non-public proceedings before the Tribunal." Paragraph 11 by contrast says that "Mr. Rebic, knowingly and wilfully interfered with the administration of justice in three respects by disclosing the identity of the protected witness," and that is disclosing to Mr. Marijacic at the newspaper, but it's disclosing the identity of the protected witness, the statement and the transcript of the witness, and the fact that the witness had testified in non-public proceedings before the Tribunal. So Mr. Marijacic is charged with publishing the statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not including the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Correct. And that's clear because paragraph 11 charges Mr. Rebic with disclosing the statement and transcript of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Akerson. I hope that has clarified the question from the Defence for Mr. Rebic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not clear, at least according to our position. May I take the floor once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly. Your Honour, when I said this was the crucial issue here, well, this has just been confirmed once again because this alleged article never included the publication of any part of the transcript or any part of the statement made by the protected witness. The alleged article refers to the witness at the period of time when he did not enjoy the status of a protected witness and it was during the investigation stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in that sense, of course, we shall have to call witnesses who will be in a position to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. So today's hearing is not for the discussion of the merit so leave it there. And shall we come back to the issue of pre-trial brief? Some -- I'd like to ask the Defence whether three weeks is sufficient for them to submit their pre-trial brief after they have received the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is Marin Ivanovic. I would like you to leave this decision until such time when we have finally received the motion from the Prosecution. Let me stress once again that we've only received the decision on the part of the Trial Chamber about our motion being rejected. So if the Prosecution provides these papers on Monday, I would ask for the Court to give us an appropriate period of time. But I believe that three weeks is not enough. It is not enough in order to prepare a proper case for the Defence, which would not be to the detriment to the rights of the Accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that the contempt hearing is to be conducted and concluded in a very swift manner, so to speak, the Chamber has in mind that we can have a trial sometime in January next year. So that's why I'm trying to speed up the preparation for trial. So, as a Pre-Trial Judge, I'd like to give the Defence a month from the day of receipt of the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, and then I'd like to encourage them to comply with that deadline. But at the end of the day, if necessary, they can ask for an extension. But we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, do you have anything to say on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, just one brief point. I would just like to point out that our clients are paying for everything themselves. I would just like to bring this to the attention of the court. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. What is it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just pointing out to Your Honour that we are having problems with funding, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are not asking a specific thing -- measure from the Chamber at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just mentioned the fact that we were having difficulties from that point of view as well, and that compromises the preparation of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Can I ask the Prosecution about the status on 68 disclosure? Is there anything to disclose there or is it -- I know it is ongoing matter but --

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: It's our intention, Your Honour, to try to disclose everything in our possession on Monday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: -- in order to try to expedite the trial date as much as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll receive the Prosecution's pre-trial brief and from the Defence in a month from that, and we'll see what we can do at that moment. There is one matter to raise with Mr. Rebic -- the Defence for Mr. Rebic, Mr. Krsnik in particular, so I have to note that Mr. Rebic has been filing his documents always confidentially, even where it would appear that there is no good reason for that. So I'd like to note at this time that -- to file the documents as confidential where it is strictly necessary. Do you follow, Mr. Rebic? I'm sorry, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do follow you, Your Honour. And you're quite right. It was the case of the last two motions or briefs, and that's the way we typed them in our office, and so it happened by chance, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And as for pre-trial brief, I emphasise once again they should be as concise as possible and as focused as possible. And I think I have exhausted my agenda that I noted down and I wonder if there is any issue to raise for the parties. Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I have two issues, Your Honour. The first issue is that regarding the disclosure on Monday, we would ask the Court to issue an oral non-disclosure order to the Defence, to prevent them from disclosing this material to persons outside the Defence team except for legitimate Defence purposes upon application to the Chamber. Some of the material is protected from other cases. Some of it pertains to ongoing investigations. And so we just need to make sure that it's not disclosed outside the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any opposition, Mr. Ivanovic and Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Marin Ivanovic speaking. We have no objections, and we believe that we have complied with this provision so far and we shall continue to comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, we always play by the Rules and we have full respect for the Court, but if we take a look at the materials, sometimes the Prosecution team wants to go beyond that, if there is no reason to keep something confidential, we don't think we should. But, of course, we shall comply with whatever decision the Court makes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is hereby so ordered but if Mr. Akerson needs a written order, could you file something in writing as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I would be happy to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And your second thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: And for this matter I need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So 66(A)(ii) materials will be disclosed to the Defence on Monday, 31st of October. At the same time, the Chamber and the Defence will receive the Prosecution's pre-trial brief. And then the Defence is ordered to submit their pre-trial briefs until Monday, 28th of November, which is one month's time from the Prosecution's submission. And then the Chamber will consider whether it will have a Pre-Trial Conference or not to get the case going for trial. The hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: [Accused and their counsel appearing by phone]
--- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
